title: Validate what the compiler cannot see
summary: Turn an unknown JSON value into a nonnegative integer or null.

scenario.briefing: A request body claims to contain a count. Validate the unknown value before the import uses it.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Use Number.isInteger and a nonnegative check.

misconceptions.feedback: Number coerces strings and other values. It does not prove the input was a number.
Interfaces are erased. Parse unknown input with explicit checks or a schema library.

sections.title: TypeScript functions and collections
sections.body: Functions declare parameter and return types, and generics preserve the relationship between them. Array<T> and ReadonlyArray<T> describe element types. Generic helpers should not fall back to any or unsafe casts.

sections.title: TypeScript errors and tools
sections.body: A type assertion does not validate runtime data. Unknown values from JSON, storage, or the network need explicit checks. tsc checks types, Vite transpiles for the browser, and ESLint or the local companion can enforce stricter rules.

statements.label: unknown forces a check before the value can be used as a number.
Type annotations remain available at runtime for validation.

steps.explanation: Types are erased at runtime. unknown plus explicit guards is the honest boundary between external data and typed code.

accessibility.summary: The TypeScript workspace is keyboard accessible. Checks verify source structure; they do not compile or run TypeScript.
